subject.title: fix(sessions): keep Matrix DM session keys case-distinct per peer

question: Should OpenClaw merge the channel-bearing Matrix DM mitigation while `per-peer` remains a documented collision-prone legacy contract, or require a compatible redesign that isolates case-distinct peers under `per-peer` too?
rationale: The patch correctly avoids silently changing a persisted channel-agnostic key shape, but deciding whether partial mitigation is acceptable for a transcript-isolation issue requires owner judgment about compatibility and security posture.

options.title: Merge scoped mitigation; retain canonical follow-up
options.body: Merge the hardening for `per-channel-peer` and `per-account-channel-peer`, explicitly keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102313 open for a separately designed `per-peer` migration.

options.title: Require full per-peer isolation first
options.body: Pause this PR until a compatibility-preserving design and migration prove that channel-agnostic `per-peer` keys cannot cross-associate case-distinct Matrix identities.

recommendation.title: Merge scoped mitigation; retain canonical follow-up
recommendation.body: Merge the hardening for `per-channel-peer` and `per-account-channel-peer`, explicitly keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102313 open for a separately designed `per-peer` migration.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shared session-key case-preservation policy and are the strongest available history-based routing candidate for its contract boundary.
